transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-05
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees (Redwood): Ava Martinez (AE), Liam Chen (SE), Jules Park (Solutions), Nora Blake (CSM)
Attendees (Customer): Dr. Maya Singh (CTO), Carlos Torres (ML Eng), Leah Kim (Product), Evan Doyle (SRE), Priyanka Rao (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed recent regression on quantized 4-bit model; discussed immediate hotfix routing and longer-term pin/rollback policies.
- Agreed to run latency tail tests and a 5% canary with fallback to older model variant.
- Security team requested SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes.

Topics: model pinning strategy, canary rollouts, fallback playbook, telemetry & tracing, security artifacts, cost vs latency tradeoffs.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, is this still Maya's window?
[00:05] Maya (Customer CTO): Yes, hi Ava, thanks. We only have 45 minutes so maybe focus on the regression and the playbook.
[00:12] Liam (Redwood SE): Cool. Quick recap from our side: over the last two days we saw a subtle quality dip when you ran the quantized q4f16 variant. Some hallucination upticks on the clinical-summarization set around long prompts, and a 12% higher 95th latency under peak.
[00:27] Carlos (ML Eng): Yeah, we noticed the same on our side. The 4-bit model was great for cost but the summaries started to omit dosage context on some long notes.
[00:33] Leah (Product): For product, this is the main blocker for rollout to primary care clinics. Can't ship if we lose dosage info occasionally.
[00:40] Ava: Understood. So we prepared two tracks: an immediate hotfix routing to prevent customer-facing impact, and a stabilization track to find a long-term pinning + rollout plan.
[00:52] Evan (SRE): Quick Q — when you say routing, you mean routing on the Redwood side not on our LB? How quick is that flip?
[00:58] Jules (Redwood Solutions): Right, we can do runtime routing policy: during the POC you can instruct the gateway to route certain request classes to a stable non-quant variant. The flip is seconds on our control plane, but there is some cache warmup on the target model (KV cache priming) so expect first-call latency to be higher.
[01:18] Priyanka (Security): Also need to note, any model switch needs to be auditable — we need change logs and the who/when for compliance.
[01:25] Nora (CSM): We'll include audit event examples in the security packet.
[01:29] Liam: For hotfix, here's a simple playbook we propose: 1) detect regression via eval set or quality monitors, 2) auto-soft-fallback: route 20% traffic to stable variant and monitor, 3) if no regressions at 95p latency and quality thresholds, escalate to 50% then 100%. The rollback can be immediate if error rate or a threshold of failed QA checks trips.
[01:51] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Question — can we pin per-customer or per-route? We have some production routes that are higher risk (oncology vs triage).
[01:58] Liam: Yes, pinning can be route-scoped or token-scoped. You can pin 'clinic-abc' to model v1.1 while 'triage' can use a newer variant. Pinning policy is in the rollout JSON we share.
[02:10] Carlos: About metrics — what telemetry do we need to trigger the soft-fallback? We have semantic similarity scores and a set of golden prompts.
[02:18] Jules: Golden prompts are perfect. We recommend combining: automated rouge/EM-like metric on the golden set plus production signals — latency P95, hallucination heuristics (named-entity drop), and manual QA flags from your triage dashboard.
[02:31] Leah: The cost delta worries us. If we pin to the larger fp16 model for high-safety routes, what's the monthly uplift?
[02:38] Ava: We'll produce a side-by-side cost table. Ballpark: quantized Q4 reduces per-token cost by ~45-60% depending on throughput; dedicated fp16 variants can be 2x token cost but give better tail latency and quality consistency. Exacts depend on burst and reserved capacity. I'll send a pricing delta after this call.
[02:56] Evan: On dedicated vs hosted: if we go dedicated, can we still use the same fallback? i.e., fallback to older model in hosted if dedicated is degraded?
[03:04] Liam: Yes, smart routing supports cross-deployment fallbacks (dedicated -> hosted compatible variant). You need network peering and routing rules; for Private/VPC there are extra controls. There's also a cold-start tradeoff if the hosted fallback has different KV cache.
[03:19] Priyanka: For KMS — do you support customer-managed keys for model logs? We can't have plaintext token data in Redwood KMS.
[03:27] Nora: We support KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include integration docs, and we can show how logs can be encrypted with your key.
[03:33] Maya: Let's walk through a concrete canary scenario. Carlos, what traffic slice can we spare?
[03:39] Carlos: We can spare 5% of triage traffic for a canary for 48h. For high-sensitivity routes it's more like 1%.
[03:45] Liam: Perfect. Proposed plan: 5% canary on triage for 48h, monitor QA metrics + P95 latency + token cost. Canary routing JSON will include fallback: if hallucination score > 0.12 or P95 > baseline + 35%, auto-fail to pinned variant.
[04:01] Leah: Who owns the auto-fail? Is that Redwood operator or customer?
[04:05] Jules: It's rule-based and can be auto-triggered by your monitor; you can choose auto or manual failover. For POCs we usually keep auto-fail enabled with conservative thresholds.
[04:15] Maya: Ok noted. On instrumentation — we need full traceability of token accounting per call; which headers provide that?
[04:22] Liam: We emit X-Redwood-Model, X-Redwood-Variant, X-Redwood-Token-Count, and request-id. We'll walk you through the tracing hook so you can correlate to your APM.
[04:33] Evan: Slight nit — some of the tokens counts seem off when we cross-check; is tokenization consistent across quantized builds?
[04:39] Liam: Tokenization is model-architecture dependent but consistent per model family. If you keep the same family and only change quantization, counts shouldn't change meaningfully. If tokenizer differences occur it's likely due to whitespace handling in prompt templates.
[04:53] Maya: Back to the regression root cause — what's the plan to stabilize the quantized variant?
[04:58] Liam: Short term: revert routing for affected routes to stable variant and run a controlled retrain/quantization pass with adjusted calibration set. Medium term: expand eval harness, include longer prompt coverage and dosage-sensitive prompts. Long term: add regression alerting based on clinical-entity retention metrics.
[05:17] Carlos: The calibration pass — is that something Redwood does or we do locally and push a new model to you?
[05:22] Liam: We can do both. For POC we can assist with a calibration sweep in our infra (using your golden prompts) under an NDA; ultimately customers often export quantization config (quant bits, calibration set) to reproduce on-prem.
[05:35] Priyanka: For compliance, we'd prefer to run quantization internally if that involves PII.
[05:40] Nora: Noted — we'll outline options: 1) Redwood runs on sanitized set; 2) you run locally and share metrics; 3) a hybrid where we provide tooling.
[05:49] Ava: Let's map immediate hotfix steps so we have a crisp runbook you can follow today.
[05:53] Ava (continues): Step 1: enable route-scoped pin to stable variant for 'clinic-primary' and 'oncology' — this prevents exposure. Step 2: trigger a 5% canary on 'triage' with fallback rules. Step 3: run 2k prompt latency/quality suite. Step 4: if canary passes, widen to 50% then 100% during business off-peak.
[06:19] Leah: For step 1 who executes the pin? Can we self-serve via console?
[06:23] Jules: Yes, we can do via Console or API. We'll share the exact curl and example JSON.
[06:29] Maya: Will the audit log show who triggered the pin and the exact config?
[06:33] Nora: Yes — audit events include actor, timestamp, old/new models, and a version diff.
[06:40] Carlos: A small note — when we switched last week the KV cache priming caused a flurry of 1k extra tokens per caller; that spiked our infra. Can we warm the cache ahead?
[06:50] Liam: You can pre-warm by running a shadow workload or using the cache priming API. We'll include scripts in the repo. Pre-warming reduces first-call latency but costs tokens to prime.
[07:01] Evan: About token accounting — we need exact token cost estimates pre/post pin. Does Redwood provide per-variant cost-per-token numbers?
[07:08] Ava: Yes, we provide model profile tables with cost per 1k tokens and expected P95 latency under a given throughput. We'll attach the profile for the variants you tested.
[07:18] Maya: Great. Next, security asks: when we do cross-deployment fallback, are logs transferred to our S3 or Redwood? We need guaranteed data residency.
[07:27] Nora: You can choose: ship logs to your S3 via secure transfer and use your KMS, or keep logs in Redwood with encryption under our KMS. For Private deployments, logs never leave your VPC unless you opt-in.
[07:40] Priyanka: We'll take Private for the pilot eval for sensitive routes. Need to see the network diagram.
[07:45] Ava: We'll send the VPC/network diagram and a checklist for peering.
[07:49] Leah: On rollback semantics, can we stage a 'read-only' shadow to compare outputs before switching?
[07:54] Jules: Yes, shadow routing is supported. You can run 100% shadow to new model and compare diffs without affecting production responses. That is how we usually run quality checks.
[08:05] Carlos: Our team will run shadow for 24h and push diffs.
[08:09] Liam: Sounds good. We also recommend adding a small sampling of human review to catch edge-cases in the 24h.
[08:15] Maya: About the golden prompt set — we think it's missing long-form discharge summaries. We'll share 500 synthetic long prompts.
[08:21] Ava: Perfect, please upload to the shared drive and we'll wire it into the eval harness.
[08:25] Leah: On canary thresholds, you mentioned hallucination score > 0.12 — what's that metric again?
[08:30] Jules: It's a heuristic we use: fraction of entity mismatches vs golden; not perfect but good signal. We'll provide the metric definition.
[08:37] Priyanka: Also please indicate which logs contain PHI and how they're redacted.
[08:42] Nora: We'll document data flow and redaction options.
[08:46] Ava: Quick run through of responsibilities: Redwood builds the pin/playbook templates and the rollback JSON; ArcticRx runs the latency and shadow tests; security gets the SOC2 + KMS notes. Anything else?
[08:59] Maya: One ask — can we get an emergency contact for after-hours rollback assistance if auto-fail doesn't trigger?
[09:06] Ava: Yes, we'll provide an escalation contact list and a phone tree for emergency ops.
[09:12] Carlos: Awesome. On benchmarks — what exact config should we use to reproduce your numbers?
[09:17] Liam: We'll publish a reproducibility doc with the exact batch sizes, sequence lengths, kernel flags, and the quantization profile. Use the same sequence length and prompt templates for parity.
[09:27] Leah: Timelines — when can we expect the calibration sweep and the canary run?
[09:31] Ava: Calibration sweep — we can start once you upload the golden prompts; expect initial results within 4 business days. Canary run — you said you'd allocate 5% triage, so earliest we can schedule is next Friday, 2025-02-14, to give time to prepare.
[09:45] Maya: Good. Anything else on open technical debt?
[09:49] Carlos: Just the tokenizer check and KV cache warm scripts.
[09:52] Liam: We'll include both.
[09:55] Ava: Okay let's recap next steps and owners (quick):
[09:58] Ava (recap): 1) Carlos to run latency suite and upload logs (due 2025-02-12). 2) Liam to provide pin/playbook JSON and rollout examples (due 2025-02-07). 3) Nora to deliver SOC2 + KMS + network diagram (due 2025-02-10). 4) Ava to send cost delta for dedicated vs hosted (due 2025-02-09). 5) Schedule canary 2025-02-14.
[10:24] Maya: That works. Thanks everyone.
[10:28] Ava: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[10:31] meeting end
